segments.text: Introduction
Hello everyone. I hope your week went well.
Today I would like to share with you a fundamental Bible story, one that many of us know, but which holds treasures of wisdom for our lives: the story of Joseph.

It is a story that beautifully reflects the reality of destiny, of God's call, and above all of the process through which He takes us. Very often we hear this phrase: “God chose you, God called you, He wants to do great things with you. » Yet, after a year, two years, or three years, we ask ourselves: “Why am I not seeing anything manifest yet? Why do I feel like promises are slow to come true? »
The answer lies in an essential spiritual truth: when God calls, there is always a process.

The Lord does not send us immediately after calling us; He first trains us to live up to our calling. A big call requires a big preparation process. When God called Moses, he had to spend forty years in the desert. For Joseph, the path to the throne began with a very special tunic.
1. The tunic of many colors: The seasons of destiny
Let's read together in Genesis chapter 37, verses 2 to 3:

“This is the seed of Jacob. Joseph, aged seventeen, shepherded the flock with his brothers; this child was with the sons of Bilhah and the sons of Zilpah, his father's wives. And Joseph reported their evil words to their father. Israel loved Joseph more than all his other sons, because he had him in his old age; and he made him a tunic of many colors. »
At only seventeen years old, Joseph received this mark of affection from his father. Remember this: you are never too young for God's calling.
Jacob gives Joseph a tunic of many colors. In your own destiny, you also wear this tunic. Why several colors? Because destiny is not linear. It is not made of a single uniform shade.
In your journey, there will be various stages:
Seasons that will make you laugh, and others that will make you cry.
Moments where you will jump for joy, and others where you will be floored.
Periods where you will be filled with strength and motivation, and others where discouragement will come knocking at your door.
Stages where you will be acclaimed, and others where you will be rejected.

By giving this tunic to his son, Jacob foreshadowed, without knowing it, the reality that Joseph would be confronted with. Even under God's love and favor, your life will not be monochrome. You will go through all the colors of your tunic.
2. The trap of dreams shared without wisdom
The text continues:
“Joseph had a dream, and he told it to his brothers, who hated him even more. »

God often speaks in dreams. Joseph, known as the dreamer, receives powerful visions of his future. But there are dreams that should not be told to just anyone, or at least not just any way. Some dreams require a lot of wisdom before being shared.

Joseph, with all the innocence and enthusiasm of his youth, tells his brothers about his dreams. He said to himself: “This is my family, my brothers, they will rejoice for me! » But his brothers saw pride and pretension in it. They asked each other: “How dare you, the least one, say that you are going to rule over us? »

Know one thing: the struggles you go through in life are not always linked to you, but to what you carry. People don't hate you for your hairstyle or your appearance; they react to the dream that God has placed in you.

Then, Joseph has a second dream where the sun, the moon and eleven stars prostrate themselves before him. This time, even his father Jacob reprimands him: “Must we come, I, your mother and your brothers, to bow down before you? »

When God reveals your destiny to you and you share it, people will often take you for someone pretentious or proud. Sometimes you will be told that it is the fruit of your imagination or that you dreamed too much. However, as long as your projects do not seem a little crazy or excessive in the eyes of the world, it is because you are not yet dreaming on the scale of God. Great dreams always create adversity. When David received the royal anointing, that's when the opposition began for him.
3. Brokenness by loved ones and Potiphar's stage

One day Jacob sent Joseph to join his brothers who were tending the flocks. It is at this precise moment that the hatred of his brothers materializes into a conspiracy. They throw him into a well with the intention of letting him die, before Ruben intervenes and they ultimately decide to sell him into slavery.
This transition directly reminds us of our Lord Jesus Christ:
Jesus came to his own people, and his own people did not receive him.
Joseph was sent to his brothers, and his brothers betrayed him.
Joseph was sold by his brothers; Jesus was delivered by one of his own.

In the school of brokenness, there is a painful truth to accept: true brokenness doesn't come from outsiders, it comes from those closest to you. It comes from those who were supposed to welcome you, support you and protect you.
Sold to merchants, Joseph arrives in Egypt in the house of Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh. And there, something extraordinary happens. Genesis 39 tells us:
“The LORD was with him, and prosperity accompanied him... His master saw that the LORD was with him. »

Do you realize what is happening here? What Joseph's own brothers, the sons of Jacob, the heirs of the covenant of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob were not able to see, a pagan Egyptian, Potiphar, saw! Sometimes people in your own home are unaware of what you are carrying, while people outside immediately detect God's grace on your life. They feel there is “something unique” about you, even if they don’t share your faith.
Potiphar sees this favor and sets Joseph over all his house. Joseph becomes the general steward, like Jesus to whom the Father entrusted everything into his hands.
4. The king's prison: The real place of the meeting

Just when everything seemed stable, tragedy strikes again. Potiphar's wife tries to seduce Joseph. Joseph refuses out of integrity towards his master and towards God. To take revenge, she falsely accuses him of rape. Potiphar believes his wife and throws Joseph into prison.

Imagine Joseph's distress: “I was hated by my brothers, sold into slavery. I was honest, I refused to sin, and here I am wrongly accused and thrown into a dungeon. » What feeling of injustice and revolt must have invaded him!
Yet the Word reminds us that all things work together for good to those who love God. And “all things” also includes false accusations, slander, rejection, and betrayals.
But Joseph is not thrown into just any dungeon: he is sent to the king's prison.

If he had remained a simple slave in the home of an ordinary citizen, he would have ended up in a common and forgotten prison. He had to pass through the house of Potiphar, a court officer, to land precisely in the prison where the king locked up his own prisoners.
It is in this prison that God awaited Joseph for his true encounter.
God does not meet you fully in your comfort zone at Jacob, or even in moments of glory at Potiphar.
God truly meets you in the king's prison.

It's in isolation, when you feel like everyone has abandoned you, that you discover who God is for you. It is in this place of solitude that Joseph realizes that he has the gift of interpreting dreams. This is where his own dreams begin to make sense. So that you no longer have any human support and learn to rely only on Him, God sometimes allows you to be totally isolated.
5. Men's forgetfulness and God's perfect timing
In prison, Joseph meets two servants of the king: the chief cupbearer and the chief baker. They both have a dream that torments them.

What is a real dream, a real dream from God? A dream is not just what one does while sleeping; This is what keeps us from sleeping. It's this inner fire, this holy dissatisfaction that pushes you to look for answers until they materialize.

Joseph interprets their dreams: the cupbearer will be restored to his duties, while the baker will be executed. Before the cupbearer leaves, Joseph slips him a word: “Remember me when you return to Pharaoh. »
But as soon as he regains his freedom, the cupbearer completely forgets Joseph.

In your desert, you will often encounter “cupbearers”: people for whom you sacrifice, for whom you pray, to whom you share the Word and whom you help to get back on their feet. But once the blessing comes into their lives, they forget you and move on.

This silence can be discouraging. You say to yourself: “I did all this for nothing. " But no ! The ingratitude of the cupbearer is a tool of God to forge in you the character of a true leader. A true leader is not used to gain recognition; he serves because he is aware of his mission, regardless of the gratitude of men.

Furthermore, forgetting the cupbearer protected Joseph. If the cupbearer had remembered him immediately, Joseph might have been released immediately to return directly to his father Jacob. Now, God had not made him go all this way to return to his starting point!

God was waiting for the right moment. Two years later, Pharaoh in turn had a dream that no one in Egypt could interpret. It is at this precise moment that God refreshes the memory of the cupbearer, who finally remembers the young Hebrew who remained in the king's prison.
Conclusion: Fulfillment of the vision

Joseph is washed, shaved, dressed, and brought before Pharaoh. He interprets the king's dream with such brilliant wisdom that Pharaoh declares: “Since God has made known to you all these things, there is no one who is as intelligent and as wise as you. »
The prisoner instantly becomes the governor of all Egypt, the most powerful person in the country after the Pharaoh.

God's plan is finally accomplished. Famine hits the region, and Joseph's brothers are forced to come to Egypt to buy wheat. They prostrate themselves before this governor whom they do not recognize, thus fulfilling, literally, the dream of the sheaves and the stars.

Adversity is never there to destroy you; she is there to position you. Your enemies and your difficulties are invisible instruments designed to bring you exactly where God expects you. Therefore you should not hate those who harm you or conspire against you. They play, without knowing it, an indispensable role in the scenario of your destiny.

True spiritual love is not manifested among those who applaud us, but among those who persecute us. It is the love of Jesus on the cross saying, “Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.” »
Final prayer
I invite you to pray where you are. You know exactly what stage of your tunic you are in today:
Are you in the pit, betrayed by your loved ones?
Are you in the house of Potiphar, managing favor in the midst of temptations?
Are you accused unjustly or confined in the solitude of the king's prison?
Are you in the season of forgetting, after having done good to those around you?
Let us bring all this before the Lord:
“Lord, I thank You for my destiny and for the tunic of many colors that You placed on my life. I understand today that my journey is not an accident, but a perfect process initiated by Your hand.
Forgive me for my moments of impatience and discouragement. Keep my heart pure through every trial. May injustices, betrayals and times of forgetting not darken my soul and transform me negatively.

Give me the strength to love my enemies and bless those who reject me, because I know they participate in my positioning. Break all pride in me and shape my character so that I am ready to bear the responsibilities You have prepared for me. I surrender to Your perfect timing.
In the name of Jesus, Amen. »
